title: Begging
note: Begging that leaves your honour whole is as good as not begging, and the books of righteousness say the body, which can reach release, is to be kept even this way. So this chapter forbids the utter renunciation that poverty ended on.

couplets.plain: If you see someone it is right to beg from, beg. If they hide what they have, the blame is theirs, not yours.
couplets.pm: The poor may beg when they find those fit to be begged from. If such people hold back, the blame falls on them and not on the beggar. The fit are those wise enough to see a need before it is spoken and give without refusing. They are rare, so he says “if you see”. A stain shows on them like dirt on white cloth.

links.quote: If you see someone it is right to beg from, beg
links.reason: Allows begging outright, given someone it is right to ask.

links.quote: the blame is theirs, not yours

couplets.plain: Begging itself is a pleasure, if what you ask for comes without pain.
couplets.pm: Begging itself brings joy, if what is begged for comes without suffering because the giver understands. The suffering lies in judging his time and place, reading his mood, winning him over, finding words to soften him, and being refused. So begging without disgrace isn’t forbidden when poverty has brought you to the edge of death.

links.reason: Begging can turn pleasant, so long as what is asked for arrives without pain.

couplets.plain: There is a beauty even in begging, standing before those with no hiding in their hearts who know what is due.
couplets.pm: Standing before those of open heart who know what honour asks of the poor, even that begging has a beauty. The poor must stand tall in decline, and such people know this and how hard the words are to say. You need only stand before them, so you escape the smallness of speaking.

links.quote: There is a beauty even in begging
links.reason: Grants begging a beauty of its own, but only before those with no hiding in their hearts.

couplets.plain: Begging is like giving, when you beg from those who don’t know how to hide even in a dream.
couplets.pm: To go to those who don’t know how to hide what they have, even in their dreams, and to beg from them, is like giving to the poor yourself. It brings no fame of its own, but it doesn’t destroy the fame you already have.

links.quote: those who don’t know how to hide even in a dream
links.reason: Praises givers who don’t know how to hide what they have, even in a dream.

couplets.plain: It is because there are people in the world who don’t hide what they have that some can stand before them and beg.
couplets.pm: Those who can’t bring themselves to speak, and beg only by standing before someone, take this up to keep themselves alive. They do it only because a few in the world give without hiding what they have. Without such people, unable to give up their honour, they would give up their lives.

couplets.plain: See those free from the misery of hiding, and all the misery of poverty ends at once.
couplets.pm: On seeing those free of the disease of hiding what they have, all the pain of poverty ends together, for those who beg without giving up their honour. Hiding is called a disease because no one needs it. At the mere sight of such people the beggar is overjoyed.

links.quote: all the misery of poverty ends at once

couplets.plain: On seeing those who give without scorn or insult, the heart is glad and rejoices deep within.
couplets.pm: When beggars see those who give without slighting them or speaking down to them, their hearts are glad and rejoice deep inside. “Without scorn” means with respect and kind words. The pain of poverty ends, and more: they feel as if all five senses had gained great joy.

links.reason: Prizes the gift that comes without scorn or insult.

links.quote: the heart is glad and rejoices deep within

couplets.plain: Without people who beg, this great cool world would be a wooden puppet going back and forth.
couplets.pm: If there were no poor who beg, the comings and goings of people in the great cool world would be like a lifeless wooden puppet moving on its strings. Those others would gain no fame or merit by giving to them, so they would have no real life.

couplets.plain: What glory would givers have, if there were none who want to beg and receive?
couplets.pm: If no one wished to go to them and beg, what fame would givers have? None. Their power to give wouldn’t show, so they would gain no fame by it. This and the last couplet say the world needs beggars.

links.quote: if there were none who want to beg and receive

couplets.plain: A beggar should not get angry. The misery of his own poverty is witness enough.
couplets.pm: When wealth fails a giver, the beggar shouldn’t rage, saying, “He won’t give to me.” That wealth doesn’t come when it is needed has no need of other witness, since his own misery proves it. So he should know from his own pain what the giver suffers to find wealth for all who beg, and not be angry.

links.quote: A beggar should not get angry
A beggar should not get angry
links.reason: Forbids bitterness at a refusal: the one who begs must not be angry.

links.quote: The misery of his own poverty is witness enough

ideaLinks.quote: there are people in the world who don’t hide what they have
all the misery of poverty ends at once
